newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt pound interbank rates slip in flush market.
newsitem.headline: Egypt pound interbank rates slip in flush market.

text.p: Overnight interbank rates on the Egyptian pound fell in a very liquid private-sector market on Thursday to between eight and 8-1/4 percent from 8-3/4 and 9-1/2 percent on Wednesday, bankers said.

The market is usually liquid on Thursday, the last trading day in the week. Bankers said the market was "swimmming in Egyptian pounds" and that public sector banks, whose end-of-year borrowing had squeezed the market last week, were probably behind the excess liquidity.
"They seem to have squared their positions and they don't need anymore money," one banker said. The government financial year ends on June 30.
Some bankers also said that public sector banks were so flush that a few were even offering rates of about 9-1/2 and 10 percent, lower than their 10-1/2 percent minimum.
"They're following the market and not leading it. They have a lot of money by the end of the year and they want to get rid of this excess cash," one banker said.
But the bankers said the lower rates were a temporary measure and that they will rise after July 1, the beginning of the new fiscal year.
The bankers said one-week deals were uncommon in the market but a few quoted rates between 8-1/4 and 9-1/2 percent compared to 8-7/8 and 9-1/2 percent on Wednesday.
